_note: Money in the game (garage/player). Prices are the parts' and cars' own (their files). Selling: sell (garage/shop.js sellValue) — worth × ratio less a share of the repairs. The shop, kits, sales, locks, the used lot and garage space: shop (docs/SHOP.md). Repairing to 100%: price × repair.perPoint × the points missing, at least repair.minimum (dents with no points missing: the minimum). The body shell repairs the same way from its own price (car.json shell.price), plus repair.breakable for each broken window or light. A part with mechanical damage (bent, leaking, worn: garage/mechanical.js) costs price × repair.mechanical more to put right (at least repair.minimum). Parts that go on a group of sockets (wheels, tyres, spacers) are bought as a set of that many. A new car costs its class's carPrices × its priceFactor (car.json).

sell._note: What a part or car sells for (garage/shop.js sellValue): what it's worth — the least of what was paid for it, its list price and its price now — × ratio, less repairShare of what it would cost to put right (its condition, dents and mechanical damage; garage/repair.js), never below floor of the ratio's share. Repairing something only to sell it never pays. A car's body (its list price less its factory parts') the same, with its body shell's repairs; each part on it as a part. conditionCurve: the old rule (condition only), for economy files without repairShare.

repair._note: garage/repair.js. A car's damage is repaired a piece at a time (the damage report's problems) or all at once. full: back to 100%, every dent out, the mechanical damage gone. quick: share of the full price; condition up to quick.condition (never down), each dent dentScale as hard (those left shallower than dentMin m gone), leaks sealed and tyres pumped up, bends and wear mechanicalKept of what they were. Mechanical damage: the part's price × its system's share (systems; mechanical for any not listed) — a corner of a per-wheel system (suspension, brake lines) a quarter of it — at least minimum, from severity of it for a slight one up to all of it at the worst. reattach: of the part's price, bolting a part that came loose or off back on (the same either way). A part's repairs together never cost more than maxOfNew of a new one. Fitting a spare from the inventory instead is free, like fitting any part.

safetyNet._note: garage/repair.js basicRepair. A car that can't carry on (data/damage.json drivable) whose player can't afford the quick repairs that would make it drivable gets a basic repair free: only what stops it, each value put inside its limit (margin of it), a wheel back on, a blown engine running again at engineCondition.

raceRewards._note: Placeholder prize money (races come later): what the balance report weighs crash repairs against.

series._note: Quest series (content kind 'series': 3–6 quests in an area). Finishing every quest in one pays a bonus once: moneyShare and xpShare of what its quests' gold medals pay, in all.

shop._note: The shop, the dealership and the used car lot (Phase 6 Step 4: garage/shop.js). Prices: a part's own (its file) or a car's (carPrices by class × its priceFactor), unless catalogue sets one. catalogue.parts / .cars: { id: { price, hidden, maker, unlock: { level, series, seriesName }, from, until (a limited-time item: only sold between them) } }. unlock: the level a part's tier or a car's class needs, unless the item has its own rule. sales: { id, name, starts, ends, discount (0–1), parts, cars, categories, tiers, classes, all } — the best one on an item counts, they don't add up. bundles: kits, each part as a set for the car (wheels: four), discount off their prices together. refund.minutes: something bought new can go back for what was paid within this, if it was never fitted and is as it came. garage: slots for cars, and extra ones for money (slotPrice × growth for each bought, at most maxExtra). confirmAbove: selling something worth this or more (or a car) asks twice. usedLot: the day's used cars (the same for everyone, from the day and seed): count, which classes by weight, mileage, wear by km, accidents, aftermarket parts by tier, and the price — the body and each part by its condition (conditionCurve) × factor.

makers._note: Who makes each part, for the shop's filter: catalogue.parts[id].maker, else parts here, else Factory for stock parts and a car's own parts, else racing for race-tier parts, else byCategory.

quests._note: World quests' rewards, entry fees and tiers (content/quests.js rewardsOf). A quest never stores money: its reward is worked out from its rating (stars and km: quest/difficulty.js, stored with the quest when it's saved or published) and these. core = (base + perKm × km, at most maxKm) × byStars[stars] × byType × byClass (the lowest class it lets in: an open quest isn't worth farming with a fast car) × (1 + rivals × npc.perRival × (npc.skillFloor + their mean skill)). Its tier (tiers: unlocked by level) = floor((stars + tierOfClass) / 2), at least 1. The entry fee is core × its tier's feeShare, and the reward is core + the fee × fee.back (winning pays the fee back on top). xp the same way from base.xp and perKm.xp (no class). Pink slips: no money and no fee, the cars are the stakes: both cars' classes at most the tier's stakeMaxClass. A run's share of the reward: data/quests.json rewards and race. farming: a quest finished more than freeRuns times within windowHours pays decay^(runs past freeRuns) of it (at least floor), money and xp.

defaults._note: a quest with no rating yet (not saved since difficulty came in): what's assumed

trackEvents._note: Track events (Phase 5 Step 3, generated tracks: track/events/). A track event's reward is a quest's (quests above: its type, km of driving — lap × laps — stars, class and rivals) × byKind for its kind of track: an official track's as it is, the day's and the week's a little more, a quick race (or a shared code) less. farming: per track code, not per event (every event on a track counts): finished more than freeRuns times within windowHours, it pays decay^(runs past freeRuns), at least floor. hourlyCap: the kinds whose pay is capped — in any hour, at most goldRuns × the event's full reward in money and xp.

simulation._note: The economy simulation (npm run economy-sim: tools/economy-sim.mjs, tools/economy/sim.mjs). A bot player starts with the starter car and startingMoney, and for hours of play does quests from a pool at its skill, crashes at a realistic rate (the crash test suite's real repair bills), repairs, and buys upgrades and cars. timing: s to get to a quest and through its intro/results (a track event: trackSeconds more, entering the track and back), and the average m/s driven at each star count. crashes: per km driven × byStars × (1 − skill × skillCut), each at one of the speeds by its weight; one at dnfAt km/h or more ends the run; an upgraded car's repairs cost more by upgradeShare × its parts' value / its own. performance: a run's score = skill × skill + car × (the car's rating against the quest's recommended, as a share) + noise, and the medal it reaches: gold, silver, bronze thresholds (+ perStar for each star past one). shopping: the bot keeps reserve back; upgrades: the part with the most rating per dollar, if it adds at least minGain; a car: one rated at least carMargin above its own. pool: the quests the bot can find (made from the seed: stars by weight, km by stars, class rules, types, rivals) and series of seriesOf of them. targets: what the report checks (docs/PROGRESSION.md); the quest pay check pools the bots' runs over payCheckSeeds (a type at a tier is only a handful of runs on one seed). The shop (Phase 6 Step 4): prices now, level locks, kits and the day's used lot as the game has them; with the garage full, the weakest car is sold.

tracks._note: Track events (Phase 5 Step 3): tracks of generated events in the pool — official, daily, weekly and quick (by weight), events by type on each (laps: lap km by stars, × laps), and how a race's rivals are set (as above). Quick races are a new track each time (a fresh code) but their pay is capped each hour.

targets._note: firstUpgradeMinutes: a medium bot's first meaningful upgrade (at least meaningfulGain rating points in one buy) within this many minutes. secondCarHours: its second car between min and max hours. repairs: a crash's full repair as a share of a typical race reward (that quest's gold) — on average at most mean, never more than max. skilledVsAverage: what a high-skill bot earns against a medium one, between min and max. stuck: runs with no quest the bot can afford and enter (at most). questPay: each quest type's income an hour within [low, high] × the median of all types (per tier). levels: a medium bot's level after the simulated hours, from min to max (better tiers open with levels: not all at once).

multiplayer._note: Multiplayer races (Phase 7 Step 2; mp/results.js payFor). Paid by the server once the results are confirmed (each run checked). A finisher's pay = (base + perKm x km, up to maxKm) x byClass[car class] x places[place - 1] x (1 + perOpponent x (players - 1), NPCs counting npcShare each) x ranked (a quick race) or unranked (a private or custom lobby) x the day's factor (after dailyFull races in a day, afterDaily). XP: base + perPlaceAbove for each finisher beaten; dnf for finishing out of the race (none for leaving). Nothing is staked or lost between players.
